title: #othello #othellobroadway #othellobway #othellorevival #denzelwashing...
transcript: So I saw Othello last night and I was definitely one of the poorest people there. That is not an exaggeration, that is data driven conjecture based on the fact that the average ticket price last week was $367. And despite the fact that it's been selling extremely well and stars Denzel Washington and Jake Gyllenhaal, I went in with very leveled expectations as it opened to lukewarm-at-best reviews and missed out on any Tony nominations. It was pretty much what I expected: good, not great, and not very memorable. It takes place in “the near future” as projected on the back wall of the stage at the top of the show, but pretty much nothing else really indicates this. The clothing is contemporary military uniforms and pretentious investment banker attire, and the stage is grey and mostly bare. I don't have any clips from inside the theater as they locked our phones in yonder pouches. Anyway, I didn't love how sparse this production felt. Minimalism with Shakespeare can be very effective and bring a specific depth or clarity to the text, but this was not minimalism in an inspired, Jamie Lloyd Sunset Boulevard kind of way. Other than the lighting design which I thought was great, it was visually underwhelming, feeling like an aesthetic more than a concept, and the rest of the production couldn't quite compensate. Let's talk about the performances: Denzel and Jake were both good and if you're going to just see them, you shouldn't be disappointed. That said, I thought the direction undercut some of their potential. For example, much of this production was comedic rather than tragic and that didn't always feel intentional. The arc of Denzel’s Othello wasn't as potent as I think it's meant to be and if you went into this production not knowing anything about Denzel Washington, this performance alone probably wouldn't make you assume that he's considered one of the greatest actors of his generation or of all time. Similarly, Jake was quite good as the puppet master Iago, but it wasn't the most memorable performance I've seen from him. The supporting cast is serviceable but very insignificantly involved compared to Denzel and Jake. Overall, I thought this was fine. I had never seen Othello before, so experiencing the story in itself was interesting, and by attending the show, I was actually able to complete the entire Broadway season. But otherwise, if you're already familiar with Othello, there isn't a huge draw here. It doesn't really do or say anything novel and I couldn't discern a point of view from this revival — it felt kinda lazy. I don't wanna say it's just a cash grab because the headliners are serious actors with well-deserved hype, but I don't think a well-conceived production is too much to expect of a show that's charging up to $921 a ticket. Anyway, if you can't make it to this production, don't fret. You're not missing too much. Just go stream Fences instead. With that, another playbill for my collection.
